$comment: Reviewed dependency advisories for apps/mobile — read by scripts/check-build-security.cjs. Every entry is build tooling that never enters the app bundle. Any new advisory, changed range/severity or changed installed version fails the gate closed until this file is re-reviewed.
review: Arena agent dependency review on 2026-11-04 (npm audit --package-lock-only, Expo SDK ~57.0.30); approved by the owner in chat the same day ("execute all these points and publish. You have full permission"). Supersedes the 2026-10-15 exception (braces/node-forge, 15 high) whose advisory set no longer matched the registry.
scope: Node-only Expo build tooling (@expo/cli, config plugins, prebuild/export, metro config). The Hermes bundle contains app sources and runtime dependencies only; none of the packages below is imported by app code.

channelNotes.eas-preview-android: EAS profile `preview`, Android, MONTEWO_INTERNAL_APK_RISK_ACCEPTED=true (internal APK, owner exception since 2026-10-15)
channelNotes.internal-ci: GitHub Actions app-android.yml / app-ios.yml with MONTEWO_BUILD_CHANNEL=internal-ci — artifacts are labelled internal/test builds (debug-signed APK/AAB unless the owner keystore secrets exist; unsigned iOS Simulator build)

deniedChannels: EAS `production` builds and anything intended for Google Play / App Store stay denied until the advisories are resolved (planned: tooling update pass + Expo SDK 58) or this file is re-reviewed by the owner.

advisories.name: deepmerge
advisories.title: deepmerge mergeObject() allows prototype poisoning of returned objects
advisories.usedBy: @expo/config (merging app config objects at build time) — Node-only

advisories.name: glob
advisories.title: Glob: AbortSignal cancellation bypass allows post-timeout filesystem traversal

advisories.name: minimatch
advisories.title: minimatch has potential denial of service via globparts amplification
advisories.usedBy: glob dependency inside the same Expo tooling — Node-only

advisories.name: node-forge
advisories.title: Forge: verifyCertificateChain() removes trusted CA certificates with the same subject from the CA store
advisories.usedBy: @expo/cli (dev-server HTTPS certificates) and @expo/code-signing-certificates (EAS/Expo CLI certificate tooling) — Node-only, never imported by app code
advisories.remediation: npm audit fix (node-forge ≥1.5, also bumps @expo/prebuild-config 57.0.10→57.0.11 and adds @expo/dom-webview/@expo/log-box; 320 lock lines) — deferred to a dedicated tooling-update pass with a full rebuild verification
